201	def bytes_per_step(opt, model, n_params, batch, seq, dim, layers):
202	    """Analytical main-memory traffic per training step (bytes, fp32).
203	
204	    weights: fwd read + bwd read           = 2 · 4N
205	    grads:   bwd write + optimizer read    = 2 · 4N
206	    params @ optimizer: read + write       = 2 · 4N
207	    state:   read + write per state tensor = 2 · 4N · S_opt
208	    activations: fwd write + bwd read      = 2 · 4 · A
209	      A ≈ batch · seq · dim · layers · k, k≈14 for attention blocks
210	      (qkv/attn-matrix/proj/mlp saves), k≈10 for mamba blocks.
211	    """
212	    k = 10 if model == "mamba" else 14
213	    acts = batch * seq * dim * layers * k
214	    s = STATE_TENSORS[opt]
215	    return 4.0 * (2 * n_params + 2 * n_params + 2 * n_params
216	                  + 2 * n_params * s + 2 * acts)

238	    """[A6-HIGH] (matmul_precision_str, use_amp, precision_label) for (opt, model).
239

241	    back to grokking_race_v2._resolve_matmul_precision on the default config (the
242	    per-model auto policy). The label is what gets drawn on the plot and chosen
243	    from _PRECISION_PEAK: fp16amp (use_amp=True) rides the bf16 carrier."""
244	    g = _g()

253	    dc = dict(g.DEFAULT_CONFIG); dc["model_type"] = model

258	def measure_pipeline(opt, model, timed_steps, tuned_configs=None,
259	                     force_precision=None, max_batch=None):
260	    import torch
261	    g = _g()
262	    data, init, n_params = _data_init(model)
263	    # [R2.4-MAXBATCH item 2] train every cell at the per-model max batch (same B
264	    # within a model, deterministic repeat-tile of the native train split). B is
265	    # chosen at the SM-saturation operating point (16384 by default — one 128-row
266	    # tile per 132 SMs; the megakernel's one-CTA-per-SM throughput is already within
267	    # ~3.5% of its 4k-batch peak there, and eager is at its utilization knee). The
268	    # wall, FLOPs/step and peak VRAM below are then all measured AT this batch.
269	    if max_batch is not None:
270	        data = _tile_train_data(data, max_batch)
271	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
272	    # [A6-HIGH] per-pipeline precision: prefer the tuner's winning precision for
273	    # this (opt, model); fall back to the auto-resolved default. Applied to EVERY
274	    # run config below so wall/AI measure the tuned precision, and the ceiling
275	    # uses that precision's peak.
276	    if tuned_configs is None:
277	        tuned_configs = _load_tuned_configs(model)
278	    mp_str, use_amp, prec_label = _resolve_precision(opt, model, tuned_configs)
279	    # [ROOFLINE-FP32] OWNER OVERRIDE: when force_precision is set (e.g. "fp32"),
280	    # pin EVERY run config to it, overriding the tuner/auto resolution. This is the
281	    # whole point of the re-measure: the decoder auto-default is bf16, which makes
282	    # _try_fused_train_step DECLINE the L3 persistent megakernel (precision gate in
283	    # grokking_race_v2: L3 fires only when resolved precision == fp32). Forcing fp32
284	    # makes decoder/vit/mamba × adamw run the TRUE L3 real fwd+bwd+opt megakernel
285	    # (validated: the run banner prints "L3-REAL fused-train path ENABLED" and the
286	    # fused_train_counter advances every step). The other 8 optimizers run
287	    # eager-fp32 + the L1 fused optimizer tail (L1 has no precision gate). Every row
288	    # is then read against the fp32 CUDA-core ceiling (66.9 TF) — the uniform basis
289	    # the old bf16 chart lacked.
290	    if force_precision is not None:
291	        mp_str, use_amp, prec_label = force_precision, False, force_precision
292	
293	    # [ROOFLINE-PATH] Verify which path ACTUALLY executes (owner: "label paths
294	    # explicitly"; don't infer from gate logic). We wrap the dispatch entry points
295	    # to count real L3 / L1 firings for THIS pipeline, and read the process-global
296	    # _FUSED_ABI_STALE flag — if it tripped, L3 silently degraded to eager and the
297	    # "L3 measurement" would secretly be eager-fp32 (wrong thing measured).
298	    _counters = {"l3": 0, "l1": 0}
299	    # [ROOFLINE-ENGINE] capture the ACTUAL GEMM engine the L3 path ran (task 2):
300	    # decoder/vit bf16 → "wgmma" (TC), mamba bf16 + any fp32 → "scalar". The engine
301	    # — NOT the requested precision — drives the row's path label, precision label,
302	    # AND compute ceiling (a scalar engine computes fp32 → 66.9 TF peak even when
303	    # the config precision string is "bf16"; without this, a scalar-executing cell's
304	    # achieved-fp32 ÷ bf16-ceiling craters its fraction ~15× silently).
305	    _last_engine = {"engine": None}
306	    _orig_l3 = g._try_fused_train_step
307	    _orig_l1 = g._try_fused_step
308	    def _wrap_l3(*a, **k):
309	        r = _orig_l3(*a, **k)
310	        if r is not None:
311	            _counters["l3"] += 1
312	            if g.LAST_L3_ENGINE is not None:
313	                _last_engine["engine"] = g.LAST_L3_ENGINE["engine"]
314	        return r
315	    def _wrap_l1(*a, **k):
316	        r = _orig_l1(*a, **k)
317	        if r:
318	            _counters["l1"] += 1
319	        return r
320	
321	    def _cfgp(steps, ee):
322	        c = _cfg(opt, model, steps, ee)
323	        c["matmul_precision"] = mp_str; c["use_amp"] = use_amp
324	        return c
325	    fn = getattr(g, {
326	        "adamw": "train_adamw", "neuralgrok": "train_neuralgrok",
327	        "grokadamw": "train_grokadamw", "supergrok": "train_supergrok",
328	        "supergrok15": "train_supergrok15", "supergrok2": "train_supergrok2",
329	        "grokfast": "train_grokfast", "muon": "train_muon", "lion": "train_lion",
330	        "looksam": "train_looksam", "prodigy": "train_prodigy"}[opt])
331	
332	    # ── pass 1: pure-train wall (eval disabled). One DISCARD run first absorbs
333	    # process-global one-time costs (cuBLAS/cuDNN handles, kernel ABI caches),
334	    # then two lengths are timed and differenced — per-run setup (model build +
335	    # state-dict load) cancels in the diff, leaving pure marginal step cost.
336	    # [ROOFLINE-PATH] the path counters wrap the dispatch entries for the WHOLE
337	    # wall pass so we record what actually ran (L3 / L1 / eager), not what the gate
338	    # would permit. use_fused stays True + the forced precision is in effect, so the
339	    # REAL megakernel is what is timed.
340	    g._try_fused_train_step = _wrap_l3
341	    g._try_fused_step = _wrap_l1
342	    # [R2.4-PEAKVRAM item 2] capture PEAK VRAM of the PRODUCTION path only. This MUST
343	    # be measured during the wall pass (use_fused=True → the real megakernel/L1 path),
344	    # NOT across the whole function: pass 3 (FLOP count) runs use_fused=False → EAGER
345	    # for every cell, and eager allocates the full activation graph while the
346	    # megakernel keeps activations CTA-local. A whole-function max_memory_allocated
347	    # would report the eager-flop-pass VRAM for the 3 adamw megakernel cells —
348	    # misrepresenting exactly the production paths this table exists to characterise.
349	    # Reset before the warmup so the reading is steady-state (warmup transients
350	    # included is fine — they ARE part of the path's footprint), capture right after
351	    # the timed walls and BEFORE pass 2/3.
352	    torch.cuda.synchronize(); torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
353	    peak_vram_bytes = None
354	    try:
355	        c = _cfgp(25, 10**9)
356	        torch.manual_seed(42)
357	        fn(c, init, *data, dev, bp=0)          # discard (warmup)
358	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
359	        walls = []
360	        for steps in (15, 15 + timed_steps):
361	            c = _cfgp(steps, 10**9)
362	            torch.manual_seed(42); torch.cuda.synchronize()
363	            t0 = time.perf_counter()
364	            fn(c, init, *data, dev, bp=0)
365	            torch.cuda.synchronize()
366	            walls.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)
367	        peak_vram_bytes = int(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated())  # production-path peak
368	    finally:
369	        g._try_fused_train_step = _orig_l3
370	        g._try_fused_step = _orig_l1
371	    wall_per_step = (walls[1] - walls[0]) / timed_steps
372	    # Steps that fired L3/L1 across the two timed runs (15 + (15+timed)).
373	    _wall_total_steps = 15 + (15 + timed_steps)
374	    l3_fired = _counters["l3"]; l1_fired = _counters["l1"]
375	    l3_engine = _last_engine["engine"]   # "wgmma" | "scalar" | None (task 2)
376	    if g._FUSED_ABI_STALE:           # the stale-ABI guard tripped → L3 degraded
377	        actual_path = "eager+L1(ABI-stale)" if l1_fired else "eager(ABI-stale)"
378	    elif l3_fired > 0:
379	        # Distinguish the directly-wired TC path from the scalar megakernel (the
380	        # owner directive's path labels): L3-TC bf16 vs L3-scalar fp32.
381	        if l3_engine == "wgmma":
382	            actual_path = "L3-TC-megakernel(wgmma)"
383	        elif l3_engine == "scalar":
384	            actual_path = "L3-scalar-megakernel"
385	        else:
386	            actual_path = "L3-real-megakernel"  # engine unknown (should not happen)
387	    elif l1_fired > 0:
388	        actual_path = "eager+L1-fused-tail"
389	    else:
390	        actual_path = "eager"
391	    # ENGINE-DRIVEN precision + ceiling (task 2): when an L3 engine actually ran, the
392	    # row's precision label and compute peak follow the ENGINE, not the requested
393	    # mp_str — wgmma computes bf16 (989 TF peak), scalar computes fp32 (66.9 TF). For
394	    # eager/L1 rows keep the requested-precision label/peak (those DO run at mp_str).
395	    eng_prec_label = prec_label
396	    if l3_engine == "wgmma":
397	        eng_prec_label = "bf16"
398	    elif l3_engine == "scalar":
399	        eng_prec_label = "fp32"
400	
401	    # ── pass 2: per-10-step series via the race's own eval hook (the owner's
402	    # tracking cadence; includes eval overhead, labelled as such).
403	    series = []
404	    last = [None]
405	    def cb(step, ta, va, tea):
406	        now = time.perf_counter()
407	        if last[0] is not None:
408	            series.append({"step": step, "wall_per_step_incl_eval":
409	                           (now - last[0]) / 10.0})
410	        last[0] = now
411	    c = _cfgp(60, 10)
412	    c["_eval_callback"] = cb
413	    torch.manual_seed(42)
414	    fn(c, init, *data, dev, bp=0)
415	
416	    # ── pass 3: FLOPs/step from torch.profiler (GEMM-registered)
417	    from torch.profiler import profile, ProfilerActivity
418	    c = _cfgp(20, 10**9)
419	    # [A6-MED] disable gradient checkpointing for the FLOP count ONLY: with
420	    # checkpointing on, every block's forward GEMMs run TWICE (once in fwd, once
421	    # recomputed in bwd), so with_flops would DOUBLE-COUNT the forward GEMM FLOPs
422	    # and overstate FLOPs/step (and thus achieved FLOP/s). The model builders
423	    # honor this key (grokking_race_v2._raw_model: gc = c.get("grad_checkpoint",
424	    # True)). Wall/AI passes keep the race's real (checkpointed) setting.
425	    c["grad_checkpoint"] = False
426	    # [ROOFLINE-FLOP-FIX] CRITICAL: disable the fused megakernel for the FLOP
427	    # count ONLY. torch.profiler(with_flops=True) counts ONLY registered aten
428	    # GEMMs/convs; a fused custom megakernel is ONE opaque kernel that registers
429	    # ZERO FLOPs. With use_fused=True on the L3 cells (decoder/vit/mamba × adamw
430	    # under forced fp32) the profiler would see ~0 FLOPs/step and crater achieved
431	    # FLOP/s for exactly the cells we are trying to measure. EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED:
432	    # decoder×adamw fp32 profiled 2.23e9 FLOPs/step with use_fused=True vs
433	    # 4.23e10 with use_fused=False (~19×). FLOPs/step is dtype- AND path-
434	    # independent (the math is identical), so the eager count is the CORRECT
435	    # FLOPs/step for the L3 megakernel; achieved = (eager-counted FLOPs)/(L3 wall)
436	    # from pass 1 is valid. Non-fused cells are unaffected (same path either way).
437	    c["use_fused"] = False
438	    torch.manual_seed(42)
439	    with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CUDA, ProfilerActivity.CPU],
440	                 with_flops=True) as prof:
441	        fn(c, init, *data, dev, bp=0)
442	    flops_total = sum(getattr(e, "flops", 0) or 0 for e in prof.key_averages())
443	    flops_per_step = flops_total / 20.0
444	
445	    dc = _cfgp(10, 10**9)
446	    batch = data[0].shape[0]
447	    # [A6-HIGH] per-model sequence length — the decoder build HARDCODES seq=4
448	    # (grokking_race_v2._raw_model: Transformer(..., 4, ...)), so the old
449	    # dc["seq_len"] (=8, the mamba chain length) over-counted decoder activation
450	    # traffic 2×. vit uses num_patches+CLS handled in-model; the activation

452	    # is 2*chain_length+2 (=8 at chain_length=3).
453	    seq = {
454	        "decoder": 4,
455	        "vit": dc.get("num_patches", 16),
456	        "mamba": 2 * dc.get("chain_length", 3) + 2,
457	    }[model]
458	    bps = bytes_per_step(opt, model, n_params, batch, seq,
459	                         dc.get("dim_model", 128), dc.get("num_layers", 2))
460	
461	    achieved = flops_per_step / wall_per_step
462	    ai = flops_per_step / bps
463	    # [A6-HIGH / task 2] Compute ceiling follows the ACTUAL engine when an L3 cell

465	    # precision for eager/L1 rows. Reading a scalar-fp32 cell against the bf16 roof

472	    _path_family = "tc" if l3_engine == "wgmma" else "scalar"

474	        "optimizer": opt, "model": model,
475	        "precision": eng_prec_label,      # task 2: label = ACTUAL engine precision
476	        "precision_requested": prec_label,  # what the config/tuner asked for
477	        "l3_engine": l3_engine,           # "wgmma" | "scalar" | None (task 2)
478	        "use_amp": bool(use_amp),
479	        # [ROOFLINE-PATH] what ACTUALLY executed during the timed wall pass (owner:

481	        # the directly-measured bf16-TC cells.
482	        "path": actual_path,
483	        "path_family": _path_family,      # "tc" (wgmma) | "scalar" (everything else)
484	        "l3_steps_fired": l3_fired,
485	        "l1_steps_fired": l1_fired,
486	        "wall_pass_total_steps": _wall_total_steps,
487	        "abi_stale": bool(g._FUSED_ABI_STALE),
488	        "steps_per_s": 1.0 / wall_per_step,
489	        "wall_per_step_ms": wall_per_step * 1e3,
490	        "flops_per_step": flops_per_step,
491	        "batch": int(batch),              # the ACTUAL train batch this row ran at
492	        # [R2.4 item 2] PEAK VRAM (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated) of the PRODUCTION

495	        "peak_vram_bytes": peak_vram_bytes,
496	        "max_batch_requested": (int(max_batch) if max_batch is not None else None),
497	        "seq_for_acts": int(seq), "dim_for_acts": int(dc.get("dim_model", 128)),
498	        "layers_for_acts": int(dc.get("num_layers", 2)),
499	        "bytes_per_step_analytical": bps,
500	        "achieved_flops_per_s": achieved,
501	        "arithmetic_intensity": ai,
502	        "matmul_peak_used": peak_c,
503	        "roofline_ceiling_flops_per_s": ceiling,
504	        "fraction_of_roofline": achieved / ceiling,
505	        "bound_regime_at_AI": bound,
506	        "achieved_bytes_per_s_analytical": bps / wall_per_step,
507	        "fraction_of_hbm_bw": (bps / wall_per_step) / PEAKS["hbm_bw"],

551	def _tc_inputs(model, B, dev):
552	    """Per-model (params, input, targets) for one TC/scalar step at batch B. The
553	    flat params are random of the TC TU's TOTAL size — step TIME is independent of
554	    param VALUES (correctness is already validated by the cells' gates: decoder
555	    13/13+5, vit 21/21, mamba 5/5), so we don't need the exact named layout here.
556	    decoder/mamba take int32 tokens [B,seq]; vit takes float32 patches [B,16,49]."""
557	    import torch
558	    mod = _build_tc_module(model)
559	    total = int(mod.TOTAL)
560	    gpar = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(42)
561	    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=gpar, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
562	    gin = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(7)
563	    if model == "vit":
564	        from tests.hw.vit_oracle import NUM_PATCHES, PATCH_DIM, VOCAB
565	        inp = torch.randn(B, NUM_PATCHES, PATCH_DIM, generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.float32)
566	        tgt = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B,), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
567	    elif model == "mamba":
568	        from tests.hw.mamba_oracle import VOCAB, P_HEAD, SEQ
569	        inp = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B, SEQ), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
570	        tgt = torch.randint(0, P_HEAD, (B,), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
571	    else:  # decoder

578	def _time_tc_kernel(call, warmup=8, iters=40):
579	    import torch
580	    for _ in range(warmup):
581	        call()
582	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
583	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
584	    for _ in range(iters):
585	        call()
586	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
587	    return (time.perf_counter() - t0) / iters

590	def measure_tc_cell(model, eager_flops_full, eager_B_full, n_params,
591	                    seq, dim, layers):
592	    """Measure the directly-loaded TC TU for `model` (Task 2) AND its scalar
593	    sibling (Task 3) at the same B%16 full batch, ncta_cap=0 (full saturation).
594	
595	    eager_flops_full / eager_B_full: FLOPs/step and batch from the eager adamw
596	    profile (pass 3 of measure_pipeline, use_fused=False — the path-independent
597	    GEMM count). FLOPs scale linearly in B, so flops_at(B) = eager_flops_full ·
598	    B / eager_B_full. Returns a list of two rows (tc, scalar) or [] if the JIT
599	    build is blocked.
600	    """
601	    import torch
602	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
603	    B = eager_B_full - (eager_B_full % 16)          # decoder TC requires B%16==0
604	    try:
605	        mod, params, inp, tgt, total = _tc_inputs(model, B, dev)
606	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — JIT blocked → owner says skip TC rows
607	        print(f"  TC[{model}] BUILD/SETUP FAILED (skipping TC rows): {e}", flush=True)
608	        return []
609	    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
610	    torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False
611	    flops_per_step = eager_flops_full * (B / float(eager_B_full))
612	    beta1, beta2 = 0.9, 0.98
613	    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2
614	    lr, eps, wd = 1e-3, 1e-8, 0.0
615	    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
616	
617	    def _tc_call():
618	        return mod.tc_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, lr, beta1, beta2,
619	                                 eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)
620	    def _sc_call():
621	        return mod.scalar_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, lr, beta1,
622	                                     beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1)
623	
624	    rows = []
625	    for label, family, prec, call, has in (
626	        ("tc_train_step",     "tc",     "bf16-TC", _tc_call, True),
627	        ("scalar_train_step", "scalar-mega", "fp32", _sc_call,
628	         hasattr(mod, "scalar_train_step")),
629	    ):
630	        if not has:
631	            continue
632	        try:
633	            wall = _time_tc_kernel(call)
634	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
635	            print(f"  TC[{model}] {label} FAILED: {e}", flush=True)
636	            continue
637	        # Bytes/AI: keep the SAME analytical traffic model as the scalar rows for
638	        # cross-row comparability (adamw S=2), BUT the TC kernel stores activations
639	        # in bf16 (2B not 4B). The activation term dominates at these B, so an
640	        # all-fp32 byte model understates TC AI ~2×. We report BOTH: the fp32-model
641	        # AI (comparable to every other row) and a TC-faithful AI (activations 2B).
642	        # CAVEAT (load-bearing): the TC point lands MEMORY-bound in this analytical
643	        # model (AI·BW < bf16 peak), so the ceiling — and thus the fraction —
644	        # depends on this byte assumption. The achieved TF/s (the honest axis) does
645	        # NOT. The writeup leads with achieved TF/s and reports BOTH AIs for TC.
646	        bps_fp32 = bytes_per_step("adamw", model, n_params, B, seq, dim, layers)
647	        # TC-faithful: halve the activation byte term (acts stored bf16).
648	        acts = B * seq * dim * layers * (10 if model == "mamba" else 14)
649	        bps_tc = bps_fp32 - 2 * 4.0 * acts + 2 * 2.0 * acts  # acts 4B→2B
650	        bps = bps_tc if family == "tc" else bps_fp32
651	        achieved = flops_per_step / wall
652	        ai = flops_per_step / bps
653	        ai_fp32model = flops_per_step / bps_fp32
654	        peak_c = PEAKS["bf16_tc"] if family == "tc" else PEAKS["fp32_cuda"]
655	        ceiling = min(peak_c, ai * PEAKS["hbm_bw"])
656	        bound = "compute" if peak_c < ai * PEAKS["hbm_bw"] else "memory"
657	        rows.append({
658	            "optimizer": "adamw", "model": model,
659	            "precision": prec, "use_amp": False,
660	            "path": f"L3-real-megakernel({label})", "path_family": family,
661	            "tc_batch": B, "ncta_cap": 0,
662	            "steps_per_s": 1.0 / wall, "wall_per_step_ms": wall * 1e3,
663	            "flops_per_step": flops_per_step,
664	            "flops_basis": "eager-profiled (use_fused=False) scaled by B/B_full",
665	            "bytes_per_step_analytical": bps,
666	            "bytes_model": ("tc-faithful (acts bf16 2B)" if family == "tc"
667	                            else "fp32 (all 4B)"),
668	            "achieved_flops_per_s": achieved,
669	            "arithmetic_intensity": ai,
670	            "arithmetic_intensity_fp32model": ai_fp32model,
671	            "matmul_peak_used": peak_c,
672	            "roofline_ceiling_flops_per_s": ceiling,
673	            "fraction_of_roofline": achieved / ceiling,
674	            "bound_regime_at_AI": bound,
675	            "achieved_bytes_per_s_analytical": bps / wall,
676	            "fraction_of_hbm_bw": (bps / wall) / PEAKS["hbm_bw"],
677	            "per10step_series_incl_eval": [],
678	        })
679	    if len(rows) >= 2:
680	        tc_r = next((r for r in rows if r["path_family"] == "tc"), None)
681	        sc_r = next((r for r in rows if r["path_family"] == "scalar-mega"), None)
682	        if tc_r and sc_r:
683	            ratio = sc_r["wall_per_step_ms"] / tc_r["wall_per_step_ms"]
684	            print(f"  TC[{model}] B={B} ncta=0  TC={tc_r['wall_per_step_ms']:.3f}ms "
685	                  f"scalar={sc_r['wall_per_step_ms']:.3f}ms  speedup(scalar/TC)="
686	                  f"{ratio:.2f}×  ({'TC wins' if ratio > 1 else 'scalar wins'})",
687	                  flush=True)
688	    return rows

781	def _delta_vs_baseline(rows, baseline_path):
782	    """[ROOFLINE-DELTA] Diff the new scalar rows against the archived eager
783	    baseline (same (optimizer, model) key, path_family scalar). Reports the change
784	    in roofline-fraction / achieved-TF/s / precision/path so the owner can see what
785	    moved when the L3 megakernel actually fired."""
786	    try:
787	        base = json.loads(Path(baseline_path).read_text())
788	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
789	        return []
790	    bmap = {(r["optimizer"], r["model"]): r
791	            for r in base.get("rows", []) if r.get("path_family", "scalar") == "scalar"}
792	    out = []
793	    for r in rows:
794	        if r.get("path_family", "scalar") != "scalar":
795	            continue                       # deltas only defined for the scalar race rows
796	        b = bmap.get((r["optimizer"], r["model"]))
797	        if not b:
798	            continue
799	        # [ROOFLINE-DELTA] Decompose WHY the fraction moved (advisor): a fraction
800	        # jump can come from (a) a real PATH change (adamw: eager+L1 → L3 real
801	        # megakernel) or (b) a pure CEILING relabel (the other opts only changed
802	        # precision bf16→fp32, dropping the ceiling 285→66.9 TF, so the same
803	        # achieved TF/s reads as a higher fraction — NOT more efficient). We record
804	        # the OLD path + a path_changed flag + the ceiling ratio so the writeup
805	        # never implies fp32 made 10 optimizers faster (it did not).
806	        # The eager baseline predates path labelling AND the extension build fix
807	        # (per the commit timeline the fused path was broken then → every baseline
808	        # row ran eager / eager+L1). So "did the PATH genuinely change" = did the
809	        # NEW row fire the L3-real megakernel (the only path this fp32-force newly
810	        # enables). The non-adamw rows ran eager+L1 in BOTH (ceiling-relabel only).
811	        path_old = b.get("path") or "eager (unlabelled pre-fix)"
812	        # A real L3 megakernel fired iff the path starts "L3-" (now "L3-TC-..."/
813	        # "L3-scalar-..." after the bf16/wgmma wiring; was "L3-real-..." pre-wiring).
814	        path_changed = str(r.get("path", "")).startswith("L3-")
815	        ceil_old = b.get("roofline_ceiling_flops_per_s", 0.0) or 0.0
816	        ceil_new = r.get("roofline_ceiling_flops_per_s", 0.0) or 0.0
817	        tf_old = b.get("achieved_flops_per_s", 0) / 1e12
818	        tf_new = r.get("achieved_flops_per_s", 0) / 1e12
819	        out.append({
820	            "optimizer": r["optimizer"], "model": r["model"],
821	            "precision_old": b.get("precision"), "precision_new": r.get("precision"),
822	            "path_old": path_old, "path_new": r.get("path"),
823	            "path_changed": path_changed,
824	            "roof_frac_old": b.get("fraction_of_roofline"),
825	            "roof_frac_new": r.get("fraction_of_roofline"),
826	            "roof_frac_delta": (r.get("fraction_of_roofline", 0)
827	                                - b.get("fraction_of_roofline", 0)),
828	            "achieved_tf_old": tf_old, "achieved_tf_new": tf_new,
829	            "achieved_tf_ratio_new_over_old": (tf_new / tf_old) if tf_old else None,
830	            "ceiling_tf_old": ceil_old / 1e12, "ceiling_tf_new": ceil_new / 1e12,
831	            "ceiling_ratio_old_over_new": (ceil_old / ceil_new) if ceil_new else None,
832	            "steps_per_s_old": b.get("steps_per_s"),
833	            "steps_per_s_new": r.get("steps_per_s"),
834	            # the honest tag: did the underlying WORK change, or just the ceiling label?
835	            "interpretation": ("PATH CHANGED (real megakernel now measured)"
836	                               if path_changed else
837	                               "ceiling-relabel only (precision changed, work same)"),
838	        })
839	    return out

166	def _time_cell(model: str, opt: str, seed: int, warmup: int, iters: int,
167	               reps: int) -> dict:
168	    os.environ["GATE_SEED"] = str(seed)
169	    import tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate as G
170	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import fused_train_step  # noqa: F401
171	    g, c, m, data, dev = G._build_cell(model)
172	    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
173	    spec = G._CELLS[f"{opt}/{model}"]
174	    opt_obj = spec["factory"](g, m.parameters(), c)
175	
176	    def _step():
177	        fused_train_step(m, opt_obj, tx, ty)
178	
179	    for _ in range(warmup):
180	        _step()
181	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
182	    medians = []
183	    for _ in range(reps):
184	        start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
185	        end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
186	        start.record()
187	        for _ in range(iters):
188	            _step()
189	        end.record()
190	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
191	        medians.append(start.elapsed_time(end) / iters)
192	    return {"model": model, "opt": opt, "seed": seed,
193	            "median_ms": statistics.median(medians),
194	            "min_ms": min(medians),
195	            "walls_ms": [round(x, 4) for x in medians]}

304	    """Median step-ms for ONE seed: inputs reseeded per-seed (params/tokens from
305	    a per-seed generator — the genuine 3-seed coverage, vs decoder_bench.measure
306	    which hardcodes seed 42). Shapes/work are identical across seeds, so this is
307	    the protocol's timing-variance probe at the d=2048 roofline (correctness +
308	    determinism are the SEPARATE fp64 gate). Mirrors roofline_bench.time_seed."""
309	    import time as _t
310	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
311	    total = int(mod.TOTAL)
312	    vocab, seq = int(mod.VOCAB), int(mod.SEQ)
313	    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
314	    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
315	    tokens = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch, seq), generator=g,
316	                           device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
317	    targets = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch,), generator=g,
318	                            device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
319	    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)

2	"""Phase 5 WS2 — ENFORCED optimizer-math single-source / drift guard.
3	
4	Three real teeth (a comment is NOT enough — this fails the build on drift):
5	
6	1. STRUCTURAL single-source (CUDA): the canonical per-element math lives once in
7	   csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h. BOTH CUDA consumers derive from it by #include:
8	     * per-op : grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/<opt>_sm90.cuh
9	     * fused  : csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh
10	   If a consumer stops #including the canonical header (i.e. reimplements the
11	   math), this FAILS — reimplementation is the only way the two CUDA trees could
12	   drift, and it is now detected.
13	
14	1b. RE-INLINE detection (Phase 5 WS3): #include alone is not enough — a consumer
15	   could keep the #include yet still LOCALLY RE-INLINE the Adam moment-update /
16	   bias-corrected apply instead of CALLING the canonical step. That silently
17	   re-introduces drift while passing the structural check. So each includable
18	   CUDA consumer (kernels/sm_90/<opt>_sm90.cuh and the fused
19	   csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh) is scanned for the Adam moment-update +
20	   apply expressions (`beta1 * exp_avg…`, `beta2 * exp_avg_sq…`, the
21	   `(m / bc1) / (sqrtf(v / bc2) + eps)` apply). Any match in a consumer FAILS —
22	   the math must come from a call into csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h, not be re-typed
23	   in the .cuh. The canonical algorithms/*.h headers themselves are NOT scanned
24	   (they are the single source and MUST contain the math); the gfx942/TPU
25	   re-expressions are the sanctioned transcriptions guarded by check (2).
26	
27	2. CONTENT-HASH manifest (drift detection for the necessary RE-EXPRESSIONS that
28	   cannot #include the C header — gfx942 transcription, TPU JAX): a committed
29	   manifest scripts/optimizer_math_manifest.json records the normalized hash of
30	   each canonical csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h. This guard recomputes the hashes and
31	   FAILS if any differs from the manifest. So editing the canonical math forces
32	   a DELIBERATE `--update-manifest` (which is the acknowledgement "I changed the
33	   canonical math and synced the gfx942/TPU re-expressions") — silent drift is
34	   impossible.
35	
36	Modes:
37	  python3 scripts/check_math_single_source.py                 # verify (exit 0/1)
38	  python3 scripts/check_math_single_source.py --update-manifest  # re-record hashes
39	The compile.py --self-test section `math_drift_guard` runs the verify path AND a
40	prove-it-triggers test (perturb canonical math in-memory → guard must flag).
41	"""

58	#
59	# The pybind entrypoints in csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp are NOT the canonical
60	# per-element math (that lives in csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h), but they ARE
61	# load-bearing glue: they own the boundary validation (check_params_grads /
62	# check_list_len), the per-param bias-correction scalar construction
63	# (bc1/bc2 = 1 - beta^step), the host-side grad clipping, and the exact

68	# body of each binding entrypoint into the manifest under "binding_regions" and

93	def _strip_comments_ws(src: str) -> str:
94	    """Normalize C/C++ source to its semantic content: drop // and /* */
95	    comments and all whitespace, so reformatting/comment edits do NOT trip the
96	    hash but any change to the actual math expressions does."""
97	    src = re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/", "", src, flags=re.DOTALL)
98	    src = re.sub(r"//[^\n]*", "", src)
99	    src = re.sub(r"\s+", "", src)
100	    return src

103	def _extract_function_body(src: str, fn_name: str) -> str:
104	    """Return the full text of `fn_name`'s definition (signature .. matching `}`).
105	
106	    Finds the DEFINITION line — a return type (`void`, `std::tuple<...>`, or
107	    `std::vector<...>`) at the start of a line followed by `fn_name(` — so a
108	    pybind `m.def("fn_name", &sg::fn_name)` registration or a forward call site
109	    is NOT mistaken for the body. Then walks from the first `{` after the
110	    signature, brace-matching (skipping braces inside // and /* */ comments and
111	    "…"/'…' literals) to the matching close. Returns "" if not found.
112	    """
113	    sig = re.compile(
114	        r"(?:^|\n)[ \t]*(?:void|std::tuple<[^>]*>|std::vector<[^>]*>)[ \t]+"
115	        + re.escape(fn_name) + r"[ \t]*\(")
116	    m = sig.search(src)
117	    if not m:
118	        return ""
119	    start = m.start() if src[m.start()] != "\n" else m.start() + 1
120	    # Find the opening brace of the body (the first '{' after the ')' that
121	    # closes the parameter list — but simply scanning for the first top-level
122	    # '{' from the signature start is sufficient here because the parameter
123	    # list contains no '{').
124	    i = m.end()
125	    n = len(src)
126	    while i < n and src[i] != "{":
127	        i += 1
128	    if i >= n:
129	        return ""
130	    depth = 0
131	    j = i
132	    in_line_comment = False
133	    in_block_comment = False
134	    in_str = None  # '"' or "'" while inside a literal
135	    while j < n:
136	        c = src[j]
137	        nxt = src[j + 1] if j + 1 < n else ""
138	        if in_line_comment:
139	            if c == "\n":
140	                in_line_comment = False
141	        elif in_block_comment:
142	            if c == "*" and nxt == "/":
143	                in_block_comment = False
144	                j += 1
145	        elif in_str is not None:
146	            if c == "\\":
147	                j += 1  # skip escaped char
148	            elif c == in_str:
149	                in_str = None
150	        elif c == "/" and nxt == "/":
151	            in_line_comment = True
152	            j += 1
153	        elif c == "/" and nxt == "*":
154	            in_block_comment = True
155	            j += 1
156	        elif c == '"' or c == "'":
157	            in_str = c
158	        elif c == "{":
159	            depth += 1
160	        elif c == "}":
161	            depth -= 1
162	            if depth == 0:
163	                return src[start:j + 1]
164	        j += 1
165	    return ""  # unbalanced — treated as "not found"
166

168	def _binding_region_hash(fn_name: str) -> str:
169	    """SHA-256 of the comment/whitespace-stripped binding-function body. Empty
170	    string hashes to a sentinel so a vanished function is DETECTED as drift
171	    (not silently skipped)."""
172	    body = _extract_function_body(_read(BINDINGS_CPP), fn_name)
173	    return hashlib.sha256(_strip_comments_ws(body).encode()).hexdigest()

181	# Phase 5 WS3 — re-inline detection.
182	#
183	# The Adam moment-update + bias-corrected decoupled-WD apply is the math that
184	# MUST live once in csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h and reach every includable CUDA
185	# consumer via a CALL (e.g. adamw_step / <opt>_adam_tail), never by being
186	# re-typed locally. These regexes match the *moment-update / apply* expressions
187	# specifically (not merely the names `beta1`/`exp_avg`, which legitimately
188	# appear as function arguments passed INTO the canonical call).
189	#
190	# Patterns (whitespace-flexible):
191	#   beta1 * exp_avg[...]        -> m  = b1*ea + (1-b1)*g   first moment update
192	#   beta2 * exp_avg_sq[...]     -> v  = b2*eas + (1-b2)*g*g second moment update
193	#   beta1 * ea... / beta2 * eas -> the quantized-state variant (ea_val/eas_val)
194	#   (... / bc1) / (sqrtf(... / bc2) ... ) -> the bias-corrected apply
195	_REINLINE_PATTERNS = [
196	    re.compile(r"beta1\s*\*\s*exp_avg\b"),
197	    re.compile(r"beta2\s*\*\s*exp_avg_sq\b"),
198	    re.compile(r"beta1\s*\*\s*ea(?:_val)?\b"),
199	    re.compile(r"beta2\s*\*\s*eas(?:_val)?\b"),
200	    re.compile(r"/\s*bc1\s*\)\s*/\s*\(\s*sqrtf\s*\(.*?/\s*bc2"),
201	]

204	# SG11 cosine-GATE re-inline detection (drift guard for the cos(grad,momentum)
205	# signal).
206	#
207	# The SG11 gate's cosine reduction — num+=g·m; den_g+=g·g; den_m+=m·m — is the
208	# canonical Sweep A (algorithms/supergrok11.h::sg11_sweep_a_step). The L3-TC staged
209	# precompute (csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stages_precompute.cuh) MUST obtain it by CALLING
210	# sg11_sweep_a_step, never by re-inlining the per-element accumulation in its own
211	# loop. A re-inlined reduction is EXACTLY how the historical cos(grad,mu) bug crept
212	# in (the loop hard-coded `den_m += u*u` with u=mu, no momentum operand). So we scan
213	# the precompute consumer for a loop-body `den_m += <x>*<x>` / `den_g += <x>*<x>`
214	# accumulation; any match FAILS — the cosine math must come from the canonical call.
215	# (The local `float num=0, den_g=0, den_m=0;` declarations + the three
216	# block_reduce_sum_f32(...) finalizers are NOT accumulations and do not match.)
217	_COSINE_REINLINE_PATTERNS = [
218	    re.compile(r"\bden_m\s*\+=\s*[\w.\[\]]+\s*\*"),
219	    re.compile(r"\bden_g\s*\+=\s*[\w.\[\]]+\s*\*"),
220	]

224	    """Headers that compute the SG11 cosine gate and MUST route the reduction

229	def scan_reinlined_cosine(path: str) -> list:
230	    """Return list of (lineno, pattern, line) for a re-inlined SG11 cosine-gate
231	    reduction in `path` (comments stripped first, so the doc lines that DESCRIBE
232	    the canonical `den_m += m·m` are ignored)."""
233	    body = _read(path)
234	    if not body:
235	        return []
236	    hits = []
237	    for lineno, raw in enumerate(body.splitlines(), 1):
238	        code = re.sub(r"//.*$", "", raw)
239	        for pat in _COSINE_REINLINE_PATTERNS:
240	            if pat.search(code):
241	                hits.append((lineno, pat.pattern, raw.strip()))
242	                break
243	    return hits

298	    "muon": "muon_update_step",
299	    "supergrok11": "sg11_sweep_b_step",
300	    "supergrok15": "sg15_sweep_b_step",
301	    # supergrok2 is intentionally absent — see SG2_SEPARATE_PATH below.
302	}
303	
304	# SuperGrok2's fused optimizer tail does NOT flow through opt_components.cuh: its
305	# CSA/HCA meta-net + sg2_apply_step live on a separate launch path
306	# (launch_csa_hca_batched_step → supergrok2.h / supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h),
307	# which opt_components.cuh itself documents (~L44). So neither `supergrok2.h`
308	# nor `sg2_apply_step` appears in this consumer by design. Asserting them here
309	# would hard-fail on the real tree; instead this is a WARNING (the include/symbol
310	# IS verified for SG2 via the per-op kernels/sm_90 structural check + the
311	# canonical-math + binding-region hashes), with a TODO to fold SG2 into the
312	# unified consumer assertion once the sibling's refactor lands.
313	SG2_SEPARATE_PATH = "supergrok2"
314	
315	
316	def _emit_warning(msg: str) -> None:
317	    """Print a clearly-labelled, non-fatal warning. Used for sub-checks that are
318	    expected to fail mid-refactor (so the guard stays usable and exits 0) but
319	    must NOT pass silently."""
320	    sys.stderr.write(f"  [WARN] {msg}\n")
321	    sys.stderr.flush()
322	
323	
324	def scan_reinlined_math(path: str) -> list:
325	    """Return list of (lineno, pattern, line) for re-inlined Adam math in `path`.
326	    Comments are stripped first so a commented-out reference line (e.g. the
327	    bit-identity doc) is not flagged."""
328	    body = _read(path)
329	    if not body:
330	        return []
331	    hits = []
332	    for lineno, raw in enumerate(body.splitlines(), 1):
333	        # drop // comments (keep code before them); the doc comments that
334	        # describe the canonical math are thereby ignored.
335	        code = re.sub(r"//.*$", "", raw)
336	        for pat in _REINLINE_PATTERNS:
337	            if pat.search(code):
338	                hits.append((lineno, pat.pattern, raw.strip()))
339	                break
340	    return hits
341	
342	
343	def normalized_math_hash(opt: str) -> str:
344	    """SHA-256 of the comment/whitespace-stripped canonical header."""
345	    body = _read(_canonical_header(opt))
346	    return hashlib.sha256(_strip_comments_ws(body).encode()).hexdigest()
347	
348	
349	def current_hashes() -> dict:
350	    return {opt: normalized_math_hash(opt) for opt in OPTS}
351	
352	
353	def update_manifest() -> int:
354	    with open(MANIFEST, "w") as f:
355	        json.dump({"_doc": "WS2 drift guard: normalized hashes of the canonical "
356	                   "csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h math (`hashes`) AND of the pybind "
357	                   "binding entrypoints in csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp "
358	                   "(`binding_regions`: boundary guards + bias-correction + "
359	                   "argument plumbing). Regenerate with `--update-manifest` ONLY "
360	                   "when intentionally changing the canonical math (and after "
361	                   "syncing the gfx942/TPU re-expressions) or the binding "
362	                   "entrypoints.",
363	                   "hashes": current_hashes(),
364	                   "binding_regions": current_binding_hashes()},
365	                  f, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
366	        f.write("\n")
367	    print(f"manifest updated: {MANIFEST}")
368	    return 0
369	
370	
371	def check(structural_only: bool = False) -> list:
372	    """Return a list of failure strings (empty = OK)."""
373	    failures = []
374	
375	    # (1) [Task #10] The eager per-op kernels/sm_90/<opt>_sm90.cuh consumers were
376	    # REMOVED (production is now a pure L3-TC megakernel, or hard-fail). Single-
377	    # source is enforced instead by (1a) the fused-consumer structural check
378	    # (opt_components.cuh #includes AND calls every canonical apply symbol), (1b)
379	    # the re-inline scan, and the canonical-math manifest hashes below — not by
380	    # per-op header inclusion. The old per-op loop is therefore intentionally gone.
381	    # (1a) fused-consumer structural hardening (WS-F5): the single fused
382	    # optimizer-tail consumer MUST #include every consumed optimizer's canonical
383	    # header AND call its apply symbol. FAIL LOUDLY if the consumer is
384	    # missing/empty (the old `if fused and …` silently disabled the whole check).
385	    fused = _read(FUSED_CONSUMER)
386	    # Comment-stripped view of the consumer for the apply-SYMBOL assertion: a
387	    # symbol name that appears ONLY inside a // or /* */ comment (e.g.
388	    # `grokadamw_step` is named in a doc comment, but the real call is
389	    # grokadamw_adam_tail) must NOT satisfy the "calls its apply symbol" check —
390	    # otherwise a dead include could be masked by a comment that merely mentions
391	    # the symbol. The #include check below still scans the raw text (an #include
392	    # is never inside a comment when active). _strip_comments_ws also drops
393	    # whitespace, which is fine: we only do substring containment on tokens.
394	    fused_code = _strip_comments_ws(fused) if fused else ""
395	    if not fused:
396	        failures.append(
397	            f"[structural] fused consumer {FUSED_CONSUMER} is missing/empty — "
398	            f"the fused optimizer-tail single-source check is disabled. Restore "
399	            f"the file.")
400	    else:
401	        for opt in OPTS:
402	            if opt == SG2_SEPARATE_PATH:
403	                # Architectural exception (separate launch path) — WARN, do not
404	                # FAIL. TODO(post-refactor): fold SG2 into this assertion once
405	                # opt_components.cuh consumes its tail.
406	                if _canonical_header(opt) not in fused:
407	                    _emit_warning(
408	                        f"{FUSED_CONSUMER} does not #include "
409	                        f"{_canonical_header(opt)} — EXPECTED: SuperGrok2's "
410	                        f"fused tail uses the separate launch_csa_hca path, not "
411	                        f"opt_components.cuh. (SG2 single-source is still "
412	                        f"covered by the per-op kernel + canonical-math + "
413	                        f"binding-region hashes.) TODO: unify post-refactor.")
414	                continue
415	            if _canonical_header(opt) not in fused:
416	                failures.append(
417	                    f"[structural] {FUSED_CONSUMER} does NOT #include the "
418	                    f"canonical {_canonical_header(opt)} (the fused tail would "
419	                    f"reimplement '{opt}' → drift). Add the #include.")
420	            # Apply-symbol assertion: include without a call is a dead include.
421	            # HARD FAIL (#19b): the in-flight opt_components.cuh refactor has
422	            # LANDED — apply_optimizer<Opt> now makes a real, distinct
423	            # algo::<sym> call for every one of the 10 non-SG2 optimizers, and
424	            # _FUSED_APPLY_SYMBOL was re-pointed to match current reality
425	            # (notably grokadamw -> grokadamw_adam_tail). So a missing call is a
426	            # genuine dead include — the fused tail silently routing '{opt}'
427	            # through a different path while the #include sits there unused — and
428	            # must break the build, not merely warn. The match is against the
429	            # COMMENT-STRIPPED consumer (fused_code) so a symbol named only in a
430	            # comment cannot satisfy this (a true-positive gate, not a textual
431	            # coincidence). The SG2 exemption above stays a WARN (separate
432	            # launch_csa_hca path).
433	            sym = _FUSED_APPLY_SYMBOL.get(opt)
434	            if sym and sym not in fused_code:
435	                failures.append(
436	                    f"[structural] {FUSED_CONSUMER} #includes "
437	                    f"{_canonical_header(opt)} but does NOT CALL its apply "
438	                    f"symbol `{sym}` (a dead include — the fused tail routes "
439	                    f"'{opt}' through a different/renamed path while the include "
440	                    f"sits unused → the single-source invariant is not actually "
441	                    f"enforced for '{opt}'). Restore the call or re-point "
442	                    f"_FUSED_APPLY_SYMBOL to the symbol the tail now calls.")
443	
444	    # (1b) re-inline detection: a consumer must CALL the canonical step, never
445	    # re-type the Adam moment-update / apply locally.
446	    for path in _consumer_headers():
447	        for lineno, pat, line in scan_reinlined_math(path):
448	            failures.append(
449	                f"[re-inline] {path}:{lineno} re-inlines canonical Adam math "
450	                f"(matched /{pat}/): `{line}`. This expression MUST come from a "
451	                f"call into csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h (e.g. <opt>_step / "
452	                f"<opt>_adam_tail), not be re-typed in the consumer.")
453	
454	    # (1c) SG11 cosine-gate re-inline detection: the staged precompute consumer MUST
455	    # obtain the cos(grad,momentum) reduction from the canonical sg11_sweep_a_step,
456	    # never re-inline `den_m += x*x` in its own loop (the path the cos(grad,mu) bug
457	    # took). Also assert it #includes the canonical supergrok11.h.
458	    for path in _cosine_consumer_headers():
459	        if _canonical_header("supergrok11") not in _read(path):
460	            failures.append(
461	                f"[structural] {path} does NOT #include the canonical "
462	                f"{_canonical_header('supergrok11')} (the SG11 cosine gate would "
463	                f"reimplement the reduction → drift). Add the #include.")
464	        for lineno, pat, line in scan_reinlined_cosine(path):
465	            failures.append(
466	                f"[cosine-re-inline] {path}:{lineno} re-inlines the SG11 cosine-gate "
467	                f"reduction (matched /{pat}/): `{line}`. The cos(grad,MOMENTUM) "
468	                f"accumulation MUST come from a call into algo::sg11_sweep_a_step "
469	                f"(csrc/algorithms/supergrok11.h), not be re-typed in the consumer "
470	                f"(re-inlining is exactly how the cos(grad,mu) bug crept in).")
471	
472	    if structural_only:
473	        return failures
474	
475	    # (2) content-hash manifest drift detection.
476	    if not os.path.exists(MANIFEST):
477	        failures.append(f"[manifest] {MANIFEST} missing — run --update-manifest.")
478	        return failures
479	    manifest_data = json.load(open(MANIFEST))
480	    recorded = manifest_data.get("hashes", {})
481	    cur = current_hashes()
482	    for opt in OPTS:
483	        if opt not in recorded:
484	            failures.append(f"[manifest] no recorded hash for {opt}.")
485	        elif recorded[opt] != cur[opt]:
486	            failures.append(
487	                f"[manifest] DRIFT: canonical csrc/algorithms/{opt}.h math "
488	                f"changed (hash {cur[opt][:12]} != recorded {recorded[opt][:12]}). "
489	                f"If intentional: sync the gfx942 transcription "
490	                f"(opt_components.hip.hpp) + TPU path, then --update-manifest.")
491	
492	    # (2b) binding-region drift detection (WS-F4): the pybind entrypoints in
493	    # bindings.cpp own the boundary guards + bias-correction + argument plumbing.
494	    recorded_bindings = manifest_data.get("binding_regions", {})
495	    cur_bindings = current_binding_hashes()
496	    for fn in BINDING_FUNCS:
497	        if fn not in recorded_bindings:
498	            failures.append(
499	                f"[binding] no recorded hash for {fn} — run --update-manifest.")
500	            continue
501	        # A vanished/renamed entrypoint hashes its empty body; surface that as a
502	        # distinct, louder message than a normal edit-drift.
503	        if not _extract_function_body(_read(BINDINGS_CPP), fn):
504	            failures.append(
505	                f"[binding] entrypoint {fn} not found in {BINDINGS_CPP} "
506	                f"(removed/renamed?). If intentional, update BINDING_FUNCS and "
507	                f"--update-manifest.")
508	        elif recorded_bindings[fn] != cur_bindings[fn]:
509	            failures.append(
510	                f"[binding] DRIFT: {BINDINGS_CPP}::{fn} changed "
511	                f"(hash {cur_bindings[fn][:12]} != recorded "
512	                f"{recorded_bindings[fn][:12]}). The binding owns the boundary "
513	                f"guards / bias-correction / list plumbing each launcher reads; "
514	                f"if the edit is intentional, --update-manifest.")
515	    return failures
516	
517	
518	def main(argv=None) -> int:
519	    argv = argv if argv is not None else sys.argv[1:]
520	    if "--update-manifest" in argv:
521	        return update_manifest()
522	    failures = check()
523	    print("=== optimizer-math drift guard (WS2, ENFORCED) ===")
524	    print(f"canonical: csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h  ({len(OPTS)} optimizers)")
525	    print(f"manifest:  {os.path.relpath(MANIFEST, ROOT)}")
526	    if failures:
527	        print("\nFAILURES:")
528	        for fr in failures:
529	            print(f"  ✗ {fr}")
530	        return 1
531	    print("\nOK — single-source structural invariant holds AND no canonical-math "
532	          "drift vs the manifest.")
533	    return 0
534	
535	
536	if __name__ == "__main__":
537	    sys.exit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""bench_backends.py — Build and profile each backend launcher with arch-native tooling.
3	
4	Outputs a single text report (default: ``bench_report.txt``) containing
5	the build log, smoke-test stdout/stderr, and a native profiler dump per
6	backend launch file. Progress is shown on stderr via a tqdm bar with ETA;
7	nothing is written to stdout except the final report path on completion.
8	
9	Profilers (auto-selected from the active backend):
10	
11	    CUDA / sm_90    → ncu (Nsight Compute) with ``--set full``,
12	                      ``--target-processes all``, source-line metrics,
13	                      ComputeWorkloadAnalysis / LaunchStats /
14	                      MemoryWorkloadAnalysis / SchedulerStats /
15	                      WarpStateStats / InstructionStats sections.
16	
17	    HIP / gfx942    → rocprof-compute (preferred) or rocprofv2 / rocprof
18	                      with ``--hip-trace --hsa-trace --stats
19	                      --basenames on --timestamp on``.
20	
21	    Pallas / TPU    → jax.profiler.start_trace / stop_trace in-process,
22	                      XLA HLO + op-level capture.
23	
24	Build:
25	    Invokes ``pip install -e .`` with ``MAX_JOBS`` set to the detected
26	    CPU-core count so the underlying torch cpp_extension build uses
27	    ninja with maximal parallelism. Build logs (nvcc / hipcc / ninja
28	    diagnostics) are captured verbatim into the report.
29	
30	Diagnostics enabled:
31	
32	    CUDA: -Xptxas=-v --resource-usage --generate-line-info -DSG_VERBOSE=1
33	    HIP:  -Rpass-analysis=kernel-resource-usage -ggdb -DSG_VERBOSE=1
34	
35	Usage:
36	    python bench_backends.py
37	    python bench_backends.py --backend cuda
38	    python bench_backends.py --output /tmp/r.txt --filter supergrok
39	    python bench_backends.py --skip-build   # reuse already-built _ops
40	"""
41	
42	from __future__ import annotations
43	
44	import argparse
45	import datetime
46	import json
47	import multiprocessing
48	import os
49	import shutil
50	import statistics
51	import subprocess
52	import sys
53	import tempfile
54	import textwrap
55	import time
56	from pathlib import Path
57	from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
58	
59	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
60	DEFAULT_REPORT = REPO_ROOT / "bench_report.txt"
61	NCPUS = multiprocessing.cpu_count()
62	
63	# (launcher_short_name, optimizer_class, source_module)
64	OPTIMIZERS: List[Tuple[str, str, str]] = [
65	    ("adamw",       "AdamW",       "grokking_optimizers"),
66	    ("grokadamw",   "GrokAdamW",   "grokking_optimizers"),
67	    ("grokfast",    "Grokfast",    "grokking_optimizers"),
68	    ("lion",        "Lion",        "grokking_optimizers"),
69	    ("looksam",     "LookSAM",     "grokking_optimizers"),
70	    ("muon",        "Muon",        "grokking_optimizers"),
71	    ("neuralgrok",  "NeuralGrok",  "grokking_optimizers"),
72	    ("prodigy",     "Prodigy",     "grokking_optimizers"),
73	    ("supergrok11", "SuperGrok11", "grokking_optimizers"),
74	    ("supergrok15", "SuperGrok15", "grokking_optimizers"),
75	    ("supergrok2",  "SuperGrok2",  "grokking_optimizers"),
76	]
77	
78	NVCC_DIAG = [
79	    "-Xptxas=-v",
80	    "--resource-usage",
81	    "--generate-line-info",
82	    "-DSG_VERBOSE=1",
83	]
84	
85	HIPCC_DIAG = [
86	    "-Rpass-analysis=kernel-resource-usage",
87	    "-ggdb",
88	    "-DSG_VERBOSE=1",
89	]
90	
91	NCU_FLAGS = [
92	    "--set", "full",
93	    "--target-processes", "all",
94	    "--import-source", "yes",
95	    "--source-folders", str(REPO_ROOT / "csrc"),
96	    "--section", "ComputeWorkloadAnalysis",
97	    "--section", "LaunchStats",
98	    "--section", "MemoryWorkloadAnalysis",
99	    "--section", "SchedulerStats",
100	    "--section", "WarpStateStats",
101	    "--section", "InstructionStats",
102	    "--section", "Occupancy",
103	]
104	
105	ROCPROF_FLAGS = [
106	    "--hip-trace",
107	    "--hsa-trace",
108	    "--stats",
109	    "--basenames", "on",
110	    "--timestamp", "on",
111	]
112	
113	
114	def detect_backend() -> str:
115	    try:
116	        import torch
117	        if torch.cuda.is_available():
118	            if hasattr(torch.version, "hip") and torch.version.hip is not None:
119	                return "hip"
120	            return "cuda"
121	    except Exception:
122	        pass
123	    try:
124	        import jax
125	        if any(d.platform == "tpu" for d in jax.devices()):
126	            return "pallas"
127	    except Exception:
128	        pass
129	    return "cuda"
130	
131	
132	def list_launchers(backend: str) -> List[Path]:
133	    if backend == "cuda":
134	        return sorted((REPO_ROOT / "csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90").glob("launch_*.cu"))
135	    if backend == "hip":
136	        cpp = list((REPO_ROOT / "csrc/backends/hip/gfx942").glob("launch_*.hip.cpp"))
137	        native = list((REPO_ROOT / "csrc/backends/hip/gfx942").glob("launch_*.hip"))
138	        return sorted(cpp + native)
139	    if backend == "pallas":
140	        return sorted((REPO_ROOT / "csrc/backends/pallas").glob("launch_*.py"))
141	    raise ValueError(f"Unknown backend: {backend}")
142	
143	
144	def section(report, title: str, char: str = "=") -> None:
145	    bar = char * 78
146	    report.write(f"\n{bar}\n {title}\n{bar}\n")
147	
148	
149	def build_extension(backend: str, report) -> bool:
150	    section(report, f"BUILD PHASE — ninja -j{NCPUS} (backend={backend})", char="=")
151	    env = os.environ.copy()
152	    env["MAX_JOBS"] = str(NCPUS)
153	    env["TORCH_CUDA_VERBOSE_BUILD"] = "1"
154	    env["NINJA_STATUS"] = "[%f/%t %es] "
155	    env["CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL"] = str(NCPUS)
156	    if backend == "cuda":
157	        env["NVCC_APPEND_FLAGS"] = " ".join(NVCC_DIAG)
158	    elif backend == "hip":
159	        env["HIPCC_COMPILE_FLAGS_APPEND"] = " ".join(HIPCC_DIAG)
160	
161	    cmd = [
162	        sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-e", ".",
163	        "--no-deps", "--force-reinstall", "-v",
164	    ]
165	    report.write(f"$ {' '.join(cmd)}\n  env.MAX_JOBS={NCPUS}\n\n")
166	    report.flush()
167	
168	    proc = subprocess.run(
169	        cmd, cwd=REPO_ROOT, env=env,
170	        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
171	        text=True,
172	    )
173	    report.write(proc.stdout or "")
174	    report.write(f"\n[build exit: {proc.returncode}]\n")
175	    return proc.returncode == 0
176	
177	
178	def make_smoke_script(opt_short: str, opt_class: str, source_module: str,
179	                      backend: str) -> str:
180	    device_pref = "tpu" if backend == "pallas" else "cuda"
181	    return textwrap.dedent(f"""
182	        import sys, traceback
183	        try:
184	            import torch
185	            from {source_module} import {opt_class}
186	            torch.manual_seed(0)
187	            device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
188	            p = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(64, 64, device=device, dtype=torch.float32))
189	            opt = {opt_class}([p], lr=1e-3)
190	            (p * p).sum().backward()
191	            opt.step()
192	            if torch.cuda.is_available():
193	                torch.cuda.synchronize()
194	            print('{opt_short}: smoke OK on', device)
195	        except Exception:
196	            traceback.print_exc()
197	            sys.exit(1)
198	    """).strip()
199	
200	
201	def write_temp_script(script: str) -> str:
202	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".py", mode="w", delete=False) as f:
203	        f.write(script)
204	        return f.name
205	
206	
207	def _child_env() -> dict:
208	    """Env for subprocess calls — ensures repo root is on PYTHONPATH so the
209	    smoke scripts can `import grokking_optimizers` without an install."""
210	    env = os.environ.copy()
211	    existing = env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
212	    env["PYTHONPATH"] = (
213	        f"{REPO_ROOT}{os.pathsep}{existing}" if existing else str(REPO_ROOT)
214	    )
215	    return env
216	
217	
218	def run_capture(cmd: List[str], report, *, timeout: int = 900,
219	                env: Optional[dict] = None) -> int:
220	    if env is None:
221	        env = _child_env()
222	    report.write(f"\n$ {' '.join(cmd)}\n")
223	    report.flush()
224	    try:
225	        proc = subprocess.run(
226	            cmd, cwd=REPO_ROOT, env=env,
227	            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
228	            text=True, timeout=timeout,
229	        )
230	        report.write(proc.stdout or "")
231	        report.write(f"\n[exit: {proc.returncode}]\n")
232	        return proc.returncode
233	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
234	        report.write(f"\n[TIMEOUT after {timeout}s]\n")
235	        report.write((exc.stdout or "") if isinstance(exc.stdout, str) else "")
236	        return -1
237	    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
238	        report.write(f"\n[command not found: {exc}]\n")
239	        return -2
240	
241	
242	def profile_cuda(script: str, report, opt_name: str) -> None:
243	    if shutil.which("ncu") is None:
244	        report.write(f"  [skip] ncu not in PATH; cannot profile {opt_name}\n")
245	        smoke_script = write_temp_script(script)
246	        try:
247	            run_capture([sys.executable, smoke_script], report)
248	        finally:
249	            os.unlink(smoke_script)
250	        return
251	
252	    smoke_script = write_temp_script(script)
253	    try:
254	        cmd = ["ncu"] + NCU_FLAGS + [sys.executable, smoke_script]
255	        run_capture(cmd, report)
256	    finally:
257	        os.unlink(smoke_script)
258	
259	
260	def profile_hip(script: str, report, opt_name: str) -> None:
261	    tool = (shutil.which("rocprof-compute")
262	            or shutil.which("rocprofv2")
263	            or shutil.which("rocprof"))
264	    smoke_script = write_temp_script(script)
265	    if tool is None:
266	        report.write("  [skip] no rocprof tool in PATH; running smoke only\n")
267	        try:
268	            run_capture([sys.executable, smoke_script], report)
269	        finally:
270	            os.unlink(smoke_script)
271	        return
272	
273	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:

337	# Realistic per-step workloads: (label, [tensor shapes]) — a transformer-ish
338	# mix of 2D weight matrices + 1D bias/norm vectors, several sizes. NOT 64x64.
339	BENCH_WORKLOADS: List[Tuple[str, List[Tuple[int, ...]]]] = [
340	    ("tiny",   [(256, 256), (256,)]),
341	    ("small",  [(1024, 1024), (1024,), (4096, 1024), (4096,)]),

347	def _percentile(samples: List[float], pct: float) -> float:
348	    """Nearest-rank percentile (pct in [0, 100]) over a list of latencies."""
349	    if not samples:
350	        return float("nan")
351	    s = sorted(samples)
352	    k = max(0, min(len(s) - 1, int(round((pct / 100.0) * (len(s) - 1)))))
353	    return s[k]

356	def _time_callable(fn: Callable[[], None], *, warmup: int, iters: int,
357	                   cuda: bool) -> List[float]:
358	    """Return a list of `iters` per-call latencies in milliseconds.
359	
360	    Warms up `warmup` times first. On CUDA uses torch.cuda.Event timing (so the
361	    async launch queue is measured correctly); on CPU uses time.perf_counter.
362	    """
363	    import torch
364	
365	    for _ in range(warmup):
366	        fn()
367	    if cuda:
368	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
369	
370	    samples: List[float] = []
371	    if cuda:
372	        for _ in range(iters):
373	            start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
374	            end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
375	            start.record()
376	            fn()
377	            end.record()
378	            torch.cuda.synchronize()
379	            samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end))   # ms
380	    else:
381	        for _ in range(iters):
382	            t0 = time.perf_counter()
383	            fn()
384	            samples.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1e3)   # ms
385	    return samples

388	def _make_params(shapes: List[Tuple[int, ...]], device: str, dtype) -> list:
389	    import torch
390	
391	    params = []
392	    for shape in shapes:
393	        p = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(*shape, device=device, dtype=dtype))
394	        p.grad = torch.randn_like(p)
395	        params.append(p)
396	    return params

399	def _refresh_grads(params: list) -> None:
400	    import torch
401	
402	    for p in params:
403	        p.grad = torch.randn_like(p)

406	# ATen baseline: stock torch.optim equivalents for the kernels we can compare
407	# against 1:1. The fused path is the project's optimizer; the baseline is the
408	# vanilla ATen implementation of the same math.

412	def _init_aten_baselines() -> None:
413	    import torch
414	
415	    ATEN_BASELINE["adamw"] = lambda params: torch.optim.AdamW(
416	        params, lr=1e-3, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-8, weight_decay=1e-2)
417	    # Lion landed in torch.optim in newer releases; fall back to None if absent.
418	    if hasattr(torch.optim, "Lion"):
419	        ATEN_BASELINE["lion"] = lambda params: torch.optim.Lion(  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
420	            params, lr=1e-4, betas=(0.9, 0.99), weight_decay=0.0)

423	def _build_fused_optimizer(opt_class: str, params: list):
424	    """Construct the project's fused optimizer; returns None (and the reason)
425	    if the extension isn't built / the class can't run on this device."""
426	    try:
427	        import grokking_optimizers as go
428	        cls = getattr(go, opt_class)
429	        return cls(params, lr=1e-3), None
430	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — surface any construction failure
431	        return None, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"

434	def run_benchmark(args, report) -> dict:
435	    """Time fused vs ATen-baseline optimizer steps over realistic shapes.
436	
437	    CPU paths run now; GPU paths only when CUDA is available. Returns a JSON-
438	    serialisable results dict (also written to `report` as text)."""
439	    try:
440	        import torch
441	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
442	        report.write(f"[bench] torch import failed: {exc}\n")
443	        return {"error": f"torch import failed: {exc}"}
444	
445	    cuda = torch.cuda.is_available()
446	    device = "cuda" if cuda else "cpu"
447	    dtype = torch.float32
448	    _init_aten_baselines()
449	
450	    results: dict = {
451	        "schema": "bench_backends/v1",
452	        "generated": datetime.datetime.now().isoformat(),
453	        "device": device,
454	        "torch": torch.__version__,
455	        "warmup": args.warmup,
456	        "iters": args.iters,
457	        "workloads": [w[0] for w in BENCH_WORKLOADS],
458	        "measurements": [],
459	    }
460	
461	    section(report, f"BENCHMARK — device={device} warmup={args.warmup} "
462	                    f"iters={args.iters}", char="=")
463	    if not cuda:
464	        report.write(
465	            "[bench] no CUDA device — timing the CPU dispatch path. GPU latency "
466	            "numbers require a real accelerator (committed baselines are env-"
467	            "specific and intentionally not checked in).\n")
468	
469	    opts = [o for o in OPTIMIZERS
470	            if not args.filter or args.filter in o[0]]
471	
472	    for opt_short, opt_class, _src in opts:
473	        for wl_name, shapes in BENCH_WORKLOADS:
474	            entry: dict = {
475	                "optimizer": opt_short,
476	                "workload": wl_name,
477	                "n_params": len(shapes),
478	                "n_elements": int(sum(_numel(s) for s in shapes)),
479	            }
480	
481	            # ── fused (project) path ──
482	            params = _make_params(shapes, device, dtype)
483	            opt, why = _build_fused_optimizer(opt_class, params)
484	            if opt is None:
485	                entry["fused"] = {"skipped": why}
486	            else:
487	                def _fused_step(_opt=opt, _params=params):
488	                    _refresh_grads(_params)
489	                    _opt.step()
490	
491	                try:
492	                    lat = _time_callable(_fused_step, warmup=args.warmup,
493	                                         iters=args.iters, cuda=cuda)
494	                    entry["fused"] = _summarize(lat, entry["n_elements"])
495	                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
496	                    entry["fused"] = {"error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}
497	
498	            # ── ATen baseline (only where a 1:1 stock optimizer exists) ──
499	            base_factory = ATEN_BASELINE.get(opt_short)
500	            if base_factory is not None:
501	                bparams = _make_params(shapes, device, dtype)
502	                try:
503	                    bopt = base_factory(bparams)
504	
505	                    def _base_step(_opt=bopt, _params=bparams):
506	                        _refresh_grads(_params)
507	                        _opt.step()
508	
509	                    blat = _time_callable(_base_step, warmup=args.warmup,
510	                                          iters=args.iters, cuda=cuda)
511	                    entry["aten_baseline"] = _summarize(blat,
512	                                                        entry["n_elements"])
513	                    # speedup = baseline_median / fused_median (>1 => fused wins)
514	                    f = entry.get("fused", {})
515	                    if "median_ms" in f and f["median_ms"] > 0:
516	                        entry["speedup_vs_aten"] = (
517	                            entry["aten_baseline"]["median_ms"] / f["median_ms"])
518	                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
519	                    entry["aten_baseline"] = {"error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}
520	
521	            results["measurements"].append(entry)
522	            _write_bench_row(report, entry)
523	
524	    return results

527	def _numel(shape: Tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
528	    n = 1
529	    for d in shape:
530	        n *= d
531	    return n

534	def _summarize(lat_ms: List[float], n_elements: int) -> dict:
535	    median = statistics.median(lat_ms)
536	    out = {
537	        "median_ms": median,
538	        "p90_ms": _percentile(lat_ms, 90),
539	        "min_ms": min(lat_ms),
540	        "samples": len(lat_ms),
541	    }
542	    # Throughput: elements updated per second at the median latency.
543	    if median > 0:
544	        out["throughput_melem_per_s"] = (n_elements / (median / 1e3)) / 1e6
545	    return out

548	def _write_bench_row(report, entry: dict) -> None:
549	    fused = entry.get("fused", {})
550	    base = entry.get("aten_baseline")
551	    line = (f"  {entry['optimizer']:<12} {entry['workload']:<7} "
552	            f"elems={entry['n_elements']:>11,} ")
553	    if "median_ms" in fused:
554	        line += (f"fused med={fused['median_ms']:.4f}ms "
555	                 f"p90={fused['p90_ms']:.4f}ms "
556	                 f"thr={fused.get('throughput_melem_per_s', 0):.1f}Melem/s")
557	    elif "skipped" in fused:
558	        line += f"fused [skip: {fused['skipped']}]"
559	    elif "error" in fused:
560	        line += f"fused [err: {fused['error']}]"
561	    if base and "median_ms" in base:
562	        line += f" | aten med={base['median_ms']:.4f}ms"
563	        if "speedup_vs_aten" in entry:
564	            line += f" speedup={entry['speedup_vs_aten']:.2f}x"
565	    report.write(line + "\n")
566	    report.flush()

1	"""wiring_check.py — OWNER BASELINE GATE: assert every routed cell's EXECUTED
2	path is the L3-TC persistent megakernel (bf16 wgmma engine), fail LOUD otherwise.
3	
4	Mandated by the locked baseline directive: "build a wiring_check.py: route every
5	cell, assert executed path == L3-TC, fail loud — saved to repo, run before every
6	roofline." This is the per-cell pass/fail oracle for the 33 (model × optimizer)
7	cells; the roofline must not be measured until this reports the converted set.
8	
9	WHAT IT DOES (no surrogate, no inference from gate logic — it OBSERVES the real
10	executed engine):
11	  * For each (model, optimizer) cell it runs a few REAL race train steps via the
12	    production train_<opt> function (grokking_race_v2.OPTIMIZER_REGISTRY), with
13	    the SAME dispatch wrapper the roofline uses to capture grokking_race_v2.
14	    LAST_L3_ENGINE — the engine dispatch.cpp ACTUALLY ran ("wgmma" | "scalar" |
15	    None). dispatch.cpp has no silent wgmma->scalar fallback, so a captured
16	    engine=="wgmma" PROVES the bf16 tensor-core L3 megakernel executed.
17	  * A cell PASSES iff every timed step fired engine=="wgmma" (path == L3-TC) AND
18	    the stale-ABI latch never tripped (a TypeError soft-degrade would mean the
19	    extension predates the widened fused_step ABI — rebuild, then re-run).
20	  * A cell is BLOCKED otherwise; the row records the OBSERVED path (eager /
21	    eager+L1-fused-tail / L3-scalar) and a cited reason so the converted/blocked
22	    table is self-documenting.
23	
24	USAGE
25	  python wiring_check.py                       # all 33 cells, table + JSON
26	  python wiring_check.py --models decoder      # subset
27	  python wiring_check.py --opts adamw,lion     # subset
28	  python wiring_check.py --require-all         # exit 1 unless ALL routed cells
29	                                               # are L3-TC (the FULL-baseline gate)
30	Default exit code: 0 if the run completed (the converted/blocked split is the
31	deliverable); --require-all makes a non-fully-converted run fail loud (exit 1),
32	which is the gate the locked directive's end-state wants green.
33	
34	Output JSON: results/h100_grokking_race/wiring_check.json
35	"""
36	from __future__ import annotations
37	
38	import argparse
39	import json
40	import sys
41	import traceback
42	from pathlib import Path
43	
44	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
45	OUT = ROOT / "results" / "h100_grokking_race"
46	
47	# The 33 cells. Optimizer keys are the RACE registry keys (note: the race uses
48	# "supergrok" for the SuperGrok11 cell; dispatch/codegen use "supergrok11" — the
49	# train fn owns the mapping, so we drive by the race key and let it translate).
50	MODELS = ["decoder", "vit", "mamba"]
51	OPTS = ["adamw", "neuralgrok", "grokadamw", "supergrok", "supergrok15",
52	        "supergrok2", "grokfast", "muon", "lion", "looksam", "prodigy"]

54	# Cited reasons a cell cannot (yet) be L3-TC. Keyed by the OBSERVED engine/path so
55	# the table explains every non-converted cell from the single source of truth
56	# (INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md verdict table + dispatch.cpp _L3_WGMMA_CELLS + the
57	# fused_train_step registries). These are diagnostic annotations, not gates — the
58	# GATE is the observed engine. A blocked cell still fails the --require-all gate.
59	_BLOCK_REASONS = {
60	    # optimizer -> short reason (why its L3-TC tail is not wired on the prod path)
61	    "looksam": ("MODEL-COUPLED: st.sam_dir needs a SAM 2nd backward in the model "
62	                "phase (INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES §6); model-stage-owned, not wired."),
63	    "supergrok": ("MODEL-COUPLED 2nd-pass (OPTSTAGES §4): SG11's `sharpness` is "
64	                  "(g_sam−g)² from a SAM SECOND backward at perturbed weights — a "

1	"""grokking_optimizers.megakernel — Stage 6 feasibility solver + generator.
2	
3	Composes the per-arch kernel primitives into one fused **L3 persistent
4	megakernel per (model × optimizer × arch)** — 3 models × 11 optimizers × 3
5	archs = 99 pipelines (§1.5 L3, §1.6 all-99, §1.8 all-three-models).
6	
7	This module is the **automatic feasibility solver** (§1.9/§1.10): it reads each
8	component's register / shared-mem (LDS on AMD) budget from the ARCH_TABLE and
9	picks the highest fusion tier that fits per (model, optimizer, arch); it falls
10	back DOWN tiers when L3 doesn't fit, and **errors** (§1.11 — no silent slow
11	path) when even the lowest tier doesn't fit. The chosen plan is what the C++
12	generator (`csrc/fused/<arch>/`) emits, and what `fused_step` in dispatch.cpp
13	prefers when a fused TU is present (§1.12).
14	
15	Hardware-deferred: the *measured* register counts come from `ptxas
16	-v`/`rocm-llvm` on real silicon; here the solver uses calibrated per-component
17	estimates (recorded in HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md), so the tier selection is
18	🟡 until the on-device register report confirms it.
19	
20	🟡 WORKSTREAM-1 CAVEAT (register-pressure reduction): the component costs below
21	were LOWERED to reflect behavior-preserving SMEM-staging / rematerialization /
22	live-range-shortening in the kernels (model_stages.cuh, supergrok2_sm90.cuh)
23	and the Hopper setmaxnreg producer/consumer warp-group split
24	(fused_megakernel.cuh). The resulting L1→L3/L2 tier promotions are ESTIMATES.
25	ptxas register allocation does NOT match this additive model — it may keep a
26	staged value live anyway, or free a slot we assumed live. The compile.py
27	per-cell `maxrregcount` sweep (knob #1) plus on-silicon `ptxas -v` are the
28	real arbiters; treat every tier change here as 🟡 until silicon confirms it.
